renders._yaml:
- component: card
  id: signature_matches
  title: Signature matches
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of signature matches, with the number of distinct proteins that have one beside it, and the bars rank the member databases that report them. It answers how much of the protein set is annotated and by which database.
    How to read: proteins without a match write no row, so compare the protein count with the input size to see the unannotated share. A database that dominates may simply be the one with the broadest signatures.
    Source: https://interproscan-docs.readthedocs.io/en/v5/OutputFormats.html
  column: entity
  aggregation: count
  aggregations:
  - nunique
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: source
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: matches, by member database
  headline: true

- component: card
  id: interpro_entries
  title: InterPro entries
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct InterPro entries the matches are integrated into, with the number of integrated matches beside it, and the ring splits those matches by member database. It answers how many distinct functions the proteins carry.
    How to read: only integrated matches count here, so a signature that InterPro has not integrated is left out. A ring led by one database shows where the curated entries come from.
    Source: https://interproscan-docs.readthedocs.io/en/v5/OutputFormats.html
  column: interpro_accession
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: source
  filter_expr: (col('interpro_accession') != '')
  caption: integrated matches, by member database

- component: figure
  title: Matches per member database
  description: |-
    Each bar counts the signature matches reported by one member database, such as Pfam, PANTHER or CDD. It answers which databases contribute annotation for these proteins.
    How to read: a tall bar is a database with many hits, and a missing one found nothing or was not run. Open the table to see the signatures and spans behind a bar.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24451626/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: source
    color: source
    labels:
      source: Member database

- component: table
  title: Signature matches table
  description: |-
    Each row is a signature match with its protein, member database, signature and description, matched span, E-value or score, and the InterPro entry, GO terms and pathways it is integrated into. It answers which domains each protein carries and where.
    How to read: sort by E-value to see the most confident matches first, and filter by database or by InterPro entry to follow one function across proteins.
    Source: https://interproscan-docs.readthedocs.io/en/v5/OutputFormats.html
